editorial:
You meet Salomé, who is tired of her routine, and Jean-Benoît, who worries about everything. With the end of the world supposedly close, their strange mood turns into a wild plan to throw a demolition party. The vibe is odd, funny, and a little sad, mixing everyday boredom with big fear. You watch two very different people try to feel alive before time runs out. The movie moves at a steady pace, giving you quiet moments and loud bursts of chaos. It feels like a hangout film with a ticking clock, where small choices matter more than huge speeches.

The acting keeps you interested, especially when the characters stop pretending and show real feelings. The party scenes are messy and fun, but some slow stretches may test your patience. If you like character dramas with dark humor, this is a good pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the party turns into full chaos as everyone destroys the house and lets go of their fears. Salomé finally seems awake and happy, while Jean-Benoît stops panicking and joins in. The twist is that the predicted end of the world does not arrive as expected; instead, the real change is personal. They walk away from the wreckage feeling lighter, realizing the party was never about the apocalypse, but about choosing to live fully before ordinary life returns.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves offbeat character dramas with dark humor.
